newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NFI 4 loss increases to PLN 11.5 mln in '96.
newsitem.headline: Polish NFI 4 loss increases to PLN 11.5 mln in '96.

text.p: The net loss of National Investment Fund (NFI) No. 4 (Progress) of Poland's mass privatisation scheme rose to 11.5 million zlotys last year from 11.1 million in 1995, the fund said in its issue prospectus.

It said the loss was mainly a result of accounting procedures under which the fund had to recalculate the depreciation for 1995 and 1996 basing it on gross value of assets rather than the net value of companies in its portfolio.
It also said the accounting changes might negatively affect its earnings in the next few years. "The consequences of the recalculation might appear over the next few years," it said.
Under the government's NFI programme, shares in about 500 mid-sized companies are allocated to 15 NFIs run by foreign and domestic management firms.

From May 12 the 26 million Poles who bought a participation unit in the scheme will have the opportunity to exchange it for 15 shares, one in each fund, which are expected to start trade on the Warsaw bourse around mid-year.
The units lose their validity on December 31, 1998.
